title: Part Fourteen: Cost of Living Over Time

sections.brief: Wages against prices 1980–2026: Israel's 1984 hyperinflation (445%) and the 1985 plan, Bank of Israel real-wage series 1996–2013, Taub's fifteen flat years, OECD average annual wages in USD PPP 2000/2010/2020/2024 for both countries, CBS average wage 2025, Census median household income 1967–2025, current inflation (Israel 1.6%, US 3.7%, Sept 2026); what the series can and cannot show. Figures: time; compare

Housing price- and rent-to-income: Israel's monthly-salaries measure (129 in 2010, 146 in 2014, 155 in 2022, with city spread), CBS dwelling index 2008–2025 (+136% real), 2025 cooling, Alrov index method, rents 2005–2011; US JCHS price-to-income 3.2/4.1/5.0, renter and owner cost burdens 2024, listed-home affordability 2019 vs 2026; why the two measures differ. Figures: compare; stats

The basket item by item: OECD price levels (food +52%, dairy +64%, cars +52%, telecom -30%), causes (tariffs, border procedures, concentration), phones (2012 Kahlon reform), childcare (free preschool from 3, 2012), college (NIS 12,017 vs $11,950 published and $2,300 net), health out-of-pocket (Taub 2011–12; KFF premiums 2025), energy and fuel (US CPI Sept 2026), household debt (NY Fed Q2 2026; BoI Q3 2025), the family budget then and now (BLS CE 1984 vs 2024; CBS HES 2010 and CPI weights 2023). Figures: compare; stats

The 2011 cottage-cheese boycott (dairy price supervision lifted 2006; ~40% rise; 25% cut on 30 June 2011), the tent protests (14 July; 3 September 400,000–460,000), the Trajtenberg Committee (appointed 8 Aug, report 26 Sept 2011) and what was implemented (taxes, free preschool from 3, competition, housing); what the OECD still found in 2025; the US record beside it. Figures: time; compare
